sentences.text: Pachydyptes is a genus of birds belonging to the class Aves, the order Sphenisciformes, and the family Spheniscidae. It is placed within the subfamily Palaeeudyptinae and contains only one species, Pachydyptes ponderosus.
G.G. Simpson estimated that this bird stood between 140 and 160 centimeters tall and weighed between 80 and possibly over 100 kilograms.
It was slightly larger than Icadyptes salasi, which is considered the best-identified of the giant penguins.
Pachydyptes was the second-tallest penguin ever known, surpassed only in height by Anthropornis nordenskjoeldi, though it was likely heavier than that species.
The genus is known from a few bones discovered in Late Eocene rocks within the Otago region of New Zealand.
These fossils were found in two clades located near the base of a phylogenetic tree.
Oliver described the genus Pachydyptes in 1930, establishing it as a valid taxonomic group.

Taxonomically, Pachydyptes belongs to the kingdom Animalia, the class Aves, the order Sphenisciformes, the family Spheniscidae, and the subfamily Palaeeudyptinae. The specific species name is Pachydyptes ponderosus.
Pachydyptes lived during the Late Eocene epoch, a time period spanning from 37 to 34 million years ago.
More precisely, the time range for this animal corresponds to the Priabonian stage, extending from 37.71 to 33.9 million years ago.
